title: Why Christians read the Torah
hook: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy in the desert and summed the law in two commandments from it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Mount Nebo, and Moses seeing the land he would never enter. Your line: seeing is enough.

Plagues and Passover. Manna and mountains. For five weeks now, this path has walked through Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. A fair question, on a Christian path: why? Most churches don't keep the food laws, and none offer animal sacrifices. Here's one place to start. When Jesus was alone in the desert, hungry and tempted three times, he answered three times. And every answer was a quotation from one book. Deuteronomy.
screen: `FIVE WEEKS IN THE BOOKS OF MOSES.` → `A FAIR QUESTION: WHY?` → `THREE ANSWERS FROM ONE BOOK.`

segments.voice: Torah is usually translated law, but it's closer to teaching, or instruction: the way a parent points a child down the right road. It's the Jewish name for the first five books of the Bible, the books of Moses. For Jesus, these were scripture; he grew up hearing them read in the synagogue. In the desert he answered the tempter with them: man shall not live by bread alone; thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God; worship God and serve him only. Near the end of his life, someone asks him which commandment is the greatest, and he reaches into the Torah twice. In Matthew's Gospel, in the King James Bible: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets." The first comes from the Shema in Deuteronomy, the line right after hear, O Israel. The second is from Leviticus. Hang: like a door on its two hinges, everything else swings on these two. Jesus also said, "Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil." Christians have understood that in different ways. Catholic, Orthodox and many Protestant teachers distinguish the moral law, which still guides, from ceremonial laws they see as fulfilled in Christ. Lutherans often speak of law and gospel, the law showing our need and the gospel meeting it. But nearly all of them read these books as their own scripture, shared with the Jewish people, who read them first.
screen: `TORAH: TEACHING, NOT JUST LAW.` · `THREE ANSWERS FROM DEUTERONOMY.` · `TWO HINGES: GOD, AND NEIGHBOR.` · `NOT TO DESTROY, BUT TO FULFIL.` · then, large: `ON THESE TWO COMMANDMENTS HANG ALL THE LAW.`

segments.voice: Hold the two hinges. On one breath, call the first to mind: love God with all your heart and soul and mind; on the next, the second: love your neighbor as yourself. Notice which one feels closer to your life today, and if you pray, ask for help with the harder one.
Torah. Hebrew for teaching or instruction, and the name for the five books of Moses that Jesus quoted and summed up in two commandments.
Your line: on these two hang all. Five books, and one door on two hinges. Day four hundred ten.

howItsDone: Most churches read from the Old Testament, including the Torah, in worship, and many Christians learn Jesus' summary of the law, the two great commandments, by heart.

what it means: the teaching of the five books of Moses, which Jesus quoted in the desert and summed up in two commandments.
what a scholar hears: Matthew 22:37–40 joins Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18; churches read the law differently, but nearly all read it as scripture.

chat.says: Christians don't keep every Old Testament law. So why read the Torah at all?
options: Jesus quoted it, and summed it up in two commandments from it: love God, love neighbor.
Mostly for its stories; Jesus himself rarely quoted from those five books.
Because it's short: the Torah is just the Ten Commandments, nothing more.
chat.meaning: Torah means teaching. Jesus answered the tempter from Deuteronomy and hung all the law on two commandments from the Torah. Nearly all Christians read it as scripture.
